judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's recomputation claims are all correct. Problem 1: consecutive angles of a rhombus are supplementary, (4x+10) + (6x+20) = 180 gives x = 15 and angles 70/110, so not a square. Problem 2: A(1,1) B(5,3) C(7,7) D(3,5) has all four sides sqrt20 and diagonals AC = sqrt72 = 8.49, BD = sqrt8 = 2.83, so rhombus and not square - and d1^2 + d2^2 = 80 = 4s^2 confirms it is a genuine rhombus. Problem 4: A(0,6) B(3,0) C(0,-2) D(-3,0) has AB = sqrt45 = 6.71 and BC = sqrt13 = 3.61; the diagonals are perpendicular but AC's midpoint (0,2) differs from BD's (0,0), so it is a kite - exactly the perpendicular-diagonals kite case the judge cites. Problem 5: 3x-5 = x+11 gives x = 8 with both diagonals 19, so rectangle and not square. Problem 6: W(-1,2) X(3,4) Y(5,0) Z(1,-2) has all sides sqrt20 and both diagonals sqrt40 = sqrt(2*20), a genuine square. All eight study-guide items check as well. What the judge did not catch is a grading-facing defect: the generated Quick Answers bank prints multi-slot answers in verify-JSON order with no labels, and that order is reversed relative to the question in two problems.

strengths_to_preserve: verify.json is the model for slot coverage in this entire shard and should be cited in SKILL.md as such. It carries several entries under the same id - a machine entry for each computed quantity plus a separate {"type": "manual"} entry for the written diagnosis of every one of the six problems. Nothing printed on the sheet is left unrecorded, and the build correctly exits 2 with six manual flags.

Problems 2 and 6 are deliberate mirror images: both are rhombi with all four sides sqrt20, but 2 has unequal diagonals (8.49 against 2.83, so rhombus only) and 6 has equal ones (6.32 = 6.32, so square). The diagonal test is therefore learned as a decision the student makes rather than a rule they recite, and problem 6 closes it by asking which single test would have ruled out 'rhombus but not square'.

Problem 4's kite is chosen so the coordinates expose the exact missing hypothesis. Sam's observation - that the diagonals are perpendicular - is TRUE and the key says so before showing that the midpoints (0,2) and (0,0) differ, so the diagnosis is 'what perpendicular diagonals alone do not guarantee' rather than 'Sam made a mistake'.

The key's grading notes name the wrong diagnosis explicitly: 'Do not accept "Priya is right, she just miscalculated" - the arithmetic was never the problem.' That is the sentence that makes an error-analysis key usable by a non-specialist grader.
The three plotting grids are printed together with the directions and each is captioned 'Grid 2 - for problem 2', so no grid can be attached to the wrong problem.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py::render_entry joins all of a problem id's expected values in verify-JSON order, comma-separated and unlabeled. When a problem asks for two named quantities and the JSON lists them in the other order, the answer key's at-a-glance grading column silently pairs the wrong value with the wrong quantity.
evidence: worksheet problem 2 asks '(a) Compute the lengths of both diagonals AC and BD'; verify.json lists BD (points [[5,3],[3,5]], 2.83) before AC ([[1,1],[7,7]], 8.49); answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '2. 2.83, 8.49'.
worksheet problem 4 asks '(a) Compute AB and BC'; verify.json lists BC (3.61) before AB (6.71); the bank prints '4. 3.61, 6.71'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry(): builds 'vals' from the entries in file order and returns '", ".join(_fmt(v) for v in vals)' - no label, no reordering.
The full worked solutions in the key print AC then BD and AB then BC correctly, so only the grading column disagrees with the question.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to take standards codes from references/standards-map.md and never to invent one, but it never says to SEARCH that file for the standard the request actually names. The result is a silent nearest-neighbour substitution plus a delivered claim that the map lacks the code - and the map's header explicitly warns against exactly this ("say so rather than reaching for the nearest one"). No gate inspects the tag, so the substitution passes every check.
evidence: final_response.md: 'references/standards-map.md has no code for quadrilateral property relationships, so every problem is tagged with the closest code the map actually contains, HSG-GPE.B.4-B.7 (coordinate geometry proofs)'.

The task contract's standard_refs are 'HSG-CO.C / HSG-SRT.B'; references/standards-map.md line 111 carries HSG-CO.A-HSG-CO.D and line 112 carries HSG-SRT.A.1-A.3, HSG-SRT.B.4-B.5. Neither was considered.

references/standards-map.md header: 'If the topic you need has no row, say so rather than reaching for the nearest one ... Add the row (with the real CCSS/AP code) in the same change as the worksheet that needed it.' The nearest-neighbour path was taken instead, and problem 3 - a pure always-true/not-always-true implication audit with no coordinates - is now tagged as a coordinate-geometry proof.

improvements.title: Label each value in a multi-slot Quick Answers entry, or bind verify-entry order to the printed sub-part order
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, stop emitting bare comma-joined values for a multi-entry id. Add an optional "slot" string to each verify entry (e.g. "AC", "BD", or "(a)", "(b)") and have render_entry print '2. AC 8.49, BD 2.83'. Where no slot is declared and an id has more than one entry, fail the quick-answers step with a message asking the author to declare slots - an unlabeled pair of numbers for a two-part question is not usable grading output. A cheaper alternative is a lint requiring the verify entries for an id to appear in the order the stem asks for them, but labeling is safer because it survives any later reordering.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture with a two-entry id whose stem asks for AC then BD while the JSON lists BD first. Assert the rendered bank does not contain the substring '2.83, 8.49' and does contain both slot labels. Against the current tree the fixture fails immediately - '2.83, 8.49' is exactly what curr-334's shipped answer key prints.
improvements.expected_impact: A grader scanning the Quick Answers column stops silently mismarking the first sub-part of every multi-part problem. Affects every sheet that puts more than one computed quantity under one problem number.
improvements.risk: Low. Labels lengthen entries, which feeds column_count() and could drop the bank from four columns to three on some sheets; the column logic already adapts and the page-budget gate would catch any overflow.

improvements.title: Search references/standards-map.md for the requested code family before substituting a different standard, and never assert the map lacks a code without searching
improvements.proposed_change: Two changes. (1) SKILL.md's tagging paragraph currently says only "a code from references/standards-map.md - never invent codes". Add the missing first step: before writing any "standard" value, do a literal substring search of references/standards-map.md for the code family the request names (HSG-CO, HSG-GMD, HSG-MG, HSN-CN, HSN-RN, HSA-REI.A, ...) and for the topic words, and use the matching row's code. Only when that search genuinely returns nothing may the sheet deviate, and the map's own header rule then applies verbatim: "say so rather than reaching for the nearest one", plus add the real row in the same change. Forbid stating in final_response.md that a code is absent from the map unless that search was actually run. (2) Add a band-consistency lint to scripts/verify.py: compare each problem's "standard" prefix with the course level the answer key declares and fail the build when a High-School sheet is tagged with a K-8 code (8.G, 7.EE, 6.EE, ...), printing the high-school rows of the map as the alternatives.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture tests/fixtures/standards_band_mismatch/: a verify JSON whose ten problems are all tagged "8.G.C.9", paired with an answer key whose declared level is "High School Geometry - Modeling with Measurement". scripts/verify.py must exit non-zero and name HSG-GMD.A.1-A.3 / HSG-MG.A.1-A.3 from the map. Run against the current tree the fixture passes silently, which is exactly how curr-345 shipped with a fully green gate chain.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a demonstrably false statement about the repository's own reference file from delivered responses, and puts the contracted standard back on the answer key's Curriculum block - the one line a parent or teacher reads to place the sheet in a course. Six of the ten cases in this shard are affected.
improvements.risk: Low. The lint is additive and fires only on a grade-prefix/course mismatch. The care point is band vocabulary: an Algebra 2 or Pre-Algebra sheet can legitimately carry an 8.EE-style code for review material, so the lint should warn rather than fail when the course string is a middle-school or transitional course.

case_summary: An excellent misconception-analysis packet and the best-verified case in my shard: verify.json records a machine entry for every computed quantity AND a manual entry for every written diagnosis, which is the pattern the rest of this shard is missing. All algebra, coordinates, diagonal comparisons and classifications are correct on independent recomputation, including the subtle problem 4 kite whose diagonals are perpendicular but do not bisect each other. Two defects the judge did not reach: the Quick Answers bank prints unlabeled multi-value entries in verify-JSON order, which is reversed relative to the question in problems 2 and 4 ('2. 2.83, 8.49' for a question asking AC then BD); and all six problems are tagged HSG-GPE.B.4-B.7 including the coordinate-free implication audit in problem 3, while the contract's HSG-CO.C sits unused in the map at line 111.
